attribution.what: Catalogue accepted an image contribution against the ASIN. No notification was sent to the brand owner, which is normal for contributions.
Conversion on the listing began separating from its 30-day trend. Sessions held; conversion fell.
Sync Integrity Monitor compared the live asset hash against the PIM canonical and flagged the mismatch. Detection lag: 41 hours.

__raw.note: Brand registry entitlement covers this ASIN, so the dispute has authority behind it — but the re-push happens first. Restoring the image does not need the dispute to resolve; the dispute stops it recurring.

attribution.what: Variation theme on the shared parent was edited by another seller on the listing, detaching two children.
Both orphaned ASINs lost the pooled review count and their positions within a day.
The family integrity map flagged the structure mismatch against the canonical theme.

__raw.note: A family rebuild restores the structure, and the pooled reviews return with it. The registry dispute matters more here than on the image, because a seller who can edit the parent can do it again next week.

live.label: Effect
live.value: Sales stopped entirely on this channel for 9 hours

live.label: Recovery
live.value: A replay restores it in one cycle — 20 minutes

attribution.what: Inventory feed cycle failed at 63% with a gateway timeout. Rows already applied stayed applied.
Walmart marked the offer out of stock, which suppressed it from search rather than showing it unavailable.
Detected on the standard 4-hour sweep. A partial-file guard would have caught this at the source.

__raw.note: This is the honest half of the story: eight of our fourteen drifts are our own pipeline, not a marketplace or a competitor. A partial-file guard on the feed writer prevents the whole class.

attribution.what: Storefront cache rebuilt from a stale product snapshot and served the old price.
No system wrote the price — which is exactly why it took a canonical comparison rather than an alert to find it.
Flagged as a price-class drift, the highest severity, because parity rules are marketplace-enforced.

__raw.note: The cheapest kind of drift to fix and the most expensive to leave: a below-canonical price on our own store is the shape of thing that costs a marketplace Buy Box.

live.label: Blast radius
live.value: 4 listings, same template — a template fix repairs all four

attribution.what: Feed template v9 shipped with the previous 72-character limit for this channel.
All four titles were overwritten with truncated values — accepted by the channel, since a short title is valid.
Detected by canonical comparison on the daily sweep. Valid-but-wrong is the hardest class to alarm on.

__raw.note: One template, four listings. Repairing the values without patching the template means the next cycle undoes the repair — which is why the slate pairs a re-push with a pipeline fix.

__raw.note: The cost here is not conversion, it is the claim. A contributed sentence we cannot substantiate is our problem the moment it is live under our brand.

Detected on the daily comparison. Medium severity, so it rides the daily repair cycle rather than interrupting.

__raw.note: Medium severity does not mean unimportant, it means predictable. This class is repaired in the daily batch, which is the whole point of severity being a field property.

stranded.cause: Feed rejected on a GTIN mismatch — the repack changed the barcode.

stranded.name: Enamel Casserole 3qt
stranded.cause: Removed by seller error during a bulk edit; the listing exists, the offer does not.

clusters.name: Attribute validation
clusters.cause: Country-of-origin was added as a required field; our mapping never included it. Every new variant fails.

clusters.name: Image URL rejected
clusters.cause: CDN signed-URL expiry is shorter than the feed retry window, so retries fetch a dead link.

clusters.name: GTIN mismatch
clusters.cause: A supplier repack changed the barcode without a new SKU. The catalogue is right and we are wrong.
